issues.legal_issue: A renewed lease obtained after a partnership has ended is not held for the former partners under the statutory constructive-trust rules when the acquiring partners were no longer under a fiduciary duty to protect the others’ interests and did not obtain the lease by using partnership assets or their former partnership status.
material_facts: The partnership was expressly limited to the term of the original lease and licence, and it ended when that term expired.
The renewed lease was granted to the defendants after the partnership had ended; the permanent licence needed to manufacture and sell salt was granted later.
No partnership funds or established partnership goodwill were used to obtain the renewed lease.
The renewed lease was granted in light of the defendants’ management and conduct, and the partners had fallen out during the final years of the partnership.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs did not establish a constructive trust under section 88 of the Indian Trusts Act. Section 90 did not apply to the case and, in any event, would not improve their position.
issues.legal_principle: Section 88 requires proof either that a person bound in a fiduciary character to protect another’s interests obtained a pecuniary advantage by availing himself of that character, or that such a person dealt in circumstances where his interests were or might be adverse to the other’s and thereby gained an advantage. The fiduciary character of partners ended with the partnership here, and the defendants did not obtain the renewed lease by using their former partnership status or partnership assets. Section 90 concerns a tenant for life, co-owner, mortgagee, or other qualified owner, and did not apply to these former partners.

rule.if: dissolved_partnership_asset_claim and partnership_ended_before_renewal and not partnership_funds_used and not partnership_goodwill_used

predicates.dissolved_partnership_asset_claim: A party to a dissolved partnership claims that a later-acquired lease is an asset of that partnership.
predicates.partnership_ended_before_renewal: The partnership ended before the disputed lease was granted, so the acquiring partners’ fiduciary relationship with the others had ended.
predicates.partnership_funds_used: Funds belonging to the partnership were used to obtain the disputed lease.
predicates.partnership_goodwill_used: Goodwill belonging to the partnership was used to obtain the disputed lease.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks to treat a later lease as an asset of a dissolved partnership, the absence of partnership funds and goodwill being used to obtain it, together with the partnership having ended first, leads to no constructive trust for the former partners.

issues.legal_issue: The presumption that a lease renewed by a partner benefits all partners is rebuttable, and the renewed lease does not benefit former partners when the circumstances show that the renewal was not intended for the dissolved partnership.
material_facts: The partnership deed fixed the partnership term to coincide with the original lease and licence and made no provision for extending the partnership or seeking a renewal for it.
The partnership had ended before the renewed lease and permanent licence were granted.
The defendants applied for renewal based on their record as lessees, and the renewal was granted in recognition of their management and conduct.
The plaintiffs tried unsuccessfully to be included among the renewed lessees.
The partners had fallen out during the final years of the partnership, and no partnership funds or goodwill were used to obtain the renewal.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances rebutted the presumption that the renewed lease should benefit all the partners; the lease was not an asset of the dissolved partnership.
issues.legal_principle: There is no absolute rule that renewal of a partnership lease by one partner must benefit all partners. There is a rebuttable presumption of fact that it will do so, depending on the circumstances. The Court considered Featherstonhaugh v. Fenwick, Clegg v. Fishwick, Clements v. Hall, Clegg v. Edmondson, In re Biss, and Griffith v. Owen, and held that the Indian Trusts Act, particularly sections 88 and 90, substantially adopted the relevant English-law principles. The partnership’s fixed term, lack of provision for renewal, absence of partnership assets or goodwill being used, the parties’ estrangement, the personal basis for the grant, and the timing of the grant rebutted the presumption.

rule.if: dissolved_partnership_asset_claim and (partnership_ended_before_renewal and no_renewal_agreement and no_partnership_assets_used and personal_qualities_supported_renewal and partners_were_estranged)

predicates.dissolved_partnership_asset_claim: A party to a dissolved partnership claims that a later-acquired lease is an asset of that partnership.
predicates.partnership_ended_before_renewal: The partnership ended before the disputed lease was granted.
predicates.no_renewal_agreement: The partnership agreement did not provide for extending the partnership or obtaining a renewed lease for it.
predicates.no_partnership_assets_used: Neither partnership funds nor partnership goodwill were used to obtain the renewed lease.
predicates.personal_qualities_supported_renewal: The renewal was granted in recognition of the acquiring parties’ own management, conduct, or other personal qualities.
predicates.partners_were_estranged: The partners were on poor terms and lacked mutual confidence during the final period of the partnership.

issues.definition: For a claim that a later lease belongs to a dissolved partnership, when the partnership ended first and the agreement, use of partnership assets, basis for renewal, and parties’ relationship indicate that renewal was not intended for the partnership, the renewed lease is not a partnership asset.
